pages.text: Chestnuts popped in the brazier ashes. Grandma rolled one onto a plate with a long stick. Yuki blew on it, peeled it, and ate. "Dinner is almost ready, so just one," Grandma said.
"We're having mountain-greens rice tonight. I'll eat two bowls!" Yuki glanced at the table, then the brazier. Another chestnut popped.
Grandma went out to tend the fire. Yuki peeled and ate one, two, three... a whole handful of chestnuts from the plate. Brown dog Momo sniffed the shells beside the brazier.
Dinner arrived, steaming. But Yuki's tummy was too full for even one spoonful. The bowl remained untouched.
Grandma rubbed Yuki's belly in circles. "Chestnuts filled it up." "But dinner's right there..." Yuki's shoulders drooped.
Grandma piled chestnuts into an empty rice bowl. "Could we put rice in here, too?" "No, the chestnuts took all the room." Yuki looked inside.
The next evening, another chestnut popped. Yuki ate just one and rested both hands on their knees. "Just One Roast Chestnut—Dinner First!"
Soon Yuki's tummy rumbled. Rice, greens, soup—yum! The bowl became empty. Momo licked their own bowl clean, too.
Yuki fixed the scarf knot and held up three fingers. Even popping chestnuts did not make the hands reach. "One, just one before dinner! Two, the rest after the meal! Three, leave room for dinner!"
Yuki proudly lifted the empty rice bowl. Grandma sat Yuki on her lap and rubbed cheeks together. Leaving tummy space made dinner much tastier. "Just One Roast Chestnut—Dinner First!"
